chapter: Chapter 1 · Water — The Essence of Life
source: NCERT Our Wondrous World (Class V), Chapter 1

overview.bigIdea: Water is everywhere, but **very little of it is fresh water we can use**. Water keeps moving – from sea to sky to land and back – and it shapes the land and gives a home to many plants and animals.

ladder.a: Only a teaspoon out of a glass is fresh
Water cycle moves water round and round

overview.languagesTitle: Three things to be able to do

languages.name: Name
languages.text: Name the forms and sources of water.

languages.name: Explain
languages.text: Explain the water cycle in 4–5 steps.

languages.name: Save
languages.text: Suggest ways to save and recharge water.

plan.text: Do the sorting and ordering activities.
Read the four lessons and flip the cards.
Check knowledge at Easy, then Hard.

lessons.title: How much water? Fresh and salt water
lessons.hook: Afreen and Jyoti watched the rain and wondered: **where does all this water come from, and where does it go?** Most of the Earth is covered with water – so why do people still run short of it?

core.def: Most water on Earth – in oceans and seas. Not fit for drinking.
Water we can drink and use for crops: rain, rivers, lakes, ponds, groundwater. Very little of Earth’s water is fresh.
If all water were a 200 ml glass, freshwater would be only 5 ml – a teaspoon!
Traditional small earthen dams in Rajasthan that collect rainwater and recharge groundwater.

explain: All living beings – people, animals, birds and plants – depend on **freshwater** for drinking, growing crops and daily work.
Ocean water is salty. In the salt pans of Gujarat it is dried to collect salt.
Wular Lake in Jammu and Kashmir is one of Asia’s largest freshwater lakes; it helps prevent floods.

example.q: Why can most of the water on Earth not be used for drinking or farming? (2 marks)
steps: Most of the water on Earth is in oceans and seas.
This water is salty, so it is not fit for drinking or for crops.
Only a very small amount is freshwater.
example.answer: Because most water is salty; only a little is fresh.

mistakes: Saying most of Earth’s water is fresh – it is salty.
Calling ocean water ‘freshwater’ because it is liquid.
lessons.tip: When asked ‘why save water?’, use the glass-and-teaspoon fact.
lessons.memory: A whole glass of water, only a spoon to drink!

cards.q: Is ocean water fresh or salty?

cards.a: Rivers, lakes, ponds, rain, groundwater (any two)

cards.q: What is dried in the salt pans of Gujarat?

lessons.title: Forms of water and the water cycle
lessons.hook: Put ice in a steel glass and watch. **Tiny drops appear on the outside!** Where did they come from? The air itself has water in it.

core.def: Solid (ice, snow, hail) · Liquid (rain, river water) · Vapour (steam, water vapour in the air).
The Sun’s heat turns water from oceans and rivers into water vapour.
Water vapour cools and forms clouds, which come down as rain, snow and hail.
The constant circular movement of water in nature.

explain: Ice melts into water; heated water becomes steam; steam cools back into water – water can change and change back.
In nature: heat → water vapour → clouds → rain/snow/hail → rivers, lakes and oceans → again.

steps: The Sun’s heat changes water from oceans and rivers into water vapour.
Water vapour cools and forms clouds.
Clouds come down as rain, snow or hail, and the water goes back into rivers, lakes and oceans. This goes on and on.
example.answer: Heat → vapour → clouds → rain → back to water bodies.

mistakes: Thinking snow is a different substance – it is solid water.
Forgetting that the water cycle never stops (it is circular).
lessons.tip: Draw a circle with 4 arrows: Sun heats → vapour rises → clouds → rain falls.
lessons.memory: Up as vapour, down as rain – round and round again!
examAsk: Name the three forms of water with examples.
Where do water drops on a cold glass come from?
Draw and label the water cycle.

cards.q: What form of water is snow?

cards.a: The constant circular movement of water in nature

play.title: Build the water cycle
play.say: Tap the steps in the right order.
items: The Sun heats water in seas and rivers
Water vapour cools and forms clouds
Clouds bring rain, snow and hail
Water flows back into rivers, lakes and oceans
play.done: That is the water cycle – and it keeps going round!

play.title: Solid, liquid or vapour?
play.say: Sort each one by its form.

lessons.title: Groundwater, surface water and rivers
lessons.hook: Pour water slowly onto soil in a glass – **it disappears!** Where does it go? Some rainwater sinks deep into the ground and waits there for us.

core.def: Water stored deep underground after rain sinks through soil and rocks. We use wells, borewells, tube wells and handpumps to get it.
Open, uncovered land, soak pits, ponds, lakes and trees help rainwater go back underground. Cemented surfaces stop it.
Water flows, stops or curves according to the shape of the land. Some rivers go to the Bay of Bengal, some to the Arabian Sea.

explain: A river often begins in the mountains and flows down across the land.
The Luni river (Rajasthan) is the only major Indian river that does not reach a sea – it ends in the Rann of Kutch.
Hiware Bazar in Maharashtra became a water-positive village through rainwater harvesting.

example.q: Why does groundwater not get recharged easily in cities? How can we help? (3 marks)
steps: Cities have many cemented surfaces like roads and paved areas.
Rainwater cannot soak into the ground through them.
We can keep open spaces, make soak pits and ponds, and plant more trees.
example.answer: Cement blocks water; open land, soak pits and trees help.

mistakes: Saying groundwater is on the surface.
Thinking all rivers flow into the same sea.
lessons.tip: Always give 2 ways to recharge groundwater – examiners love solutions.

cards.q: Name two ways to draw groundwater.
cards.a: Wells, borewells, tube wells, handpumps (any two)

cards.q: Which river does not reach a sea?

cards.a: Water flows from higher to lower ground following the land’s shape

play.title: Helps or blocks recharge?
play.say: Does it help rainwater go underground, or block it?

lessons.title: Life in water
lessons.hook: After the rain, the pond near school was full. **Tiny fish swam, and a frog sat on a lotus leaf!** Plants and animals in water have special features that help them live there.

core.def: Have features like fins to swim; many cannot live out of water.
Floating (water hyacinth), rooted floating (lotus, water lily), edge plants (reeds), plants under water.
Makes leaves waterproof so too much water does not enter the plant.
Living beings depend on each other for food – small fish, big fish, birds, otters, crocodiles.

explain: Information card: dragonfly eats mosquitoes; water scorpion breathes using a tail tube; pond heron stands still to catch fish; freshwater turtle is soft-shelled; water snake is harmless.
Keibul Lamjao (Manipur) – the only floating national park; phumdis and Sangai deer. The fishing cat has partially webbed paws.

example.q: How are lotus plants suited to living in water? (2 marks)
steps: Their flowers and leaves float on the water while their roots stay in the pond bed.
The leaves have a waxy coating that keeps them waterproof.
example.answer: Floating leaves, roots in the bed, waxy coat.

mistakes: Calling the water hyacinth a rooted plant – it is free-floating.
Forgetting that all these depend on freshwater.
lessons.tip: For ‘how is it adapted’ questions, name the body part and its job.
lessons.memory: Fins to swim, wax to stay dry, long legs to catch the fish nearby!
examAsk: Give two features of animals that live in water.
What happens if one animal in a food chain disappears?

cards.q: How does a water scorpion breathe?

play.title: Pond pals
play.say: Match each living being with its special feature.
pairs: Long legs, stands still to catch fish
Floats, roots in the pond bed

formulas.name: Freshwater
formulas.f: Only a teaspoon (5 ml) out of a 200 ml glass

formulas.name: Groundwater
formulas.f: Rain sinks through soil and rocks

formulas.name: Rivers
formulas.unit: Bay of Bengal or Arabian Sea; Luni ends in Rann of Kutch

revision: Most water on Earth is **salty**; very little is **fresh**.
**Water cycle:** heat → vapour → clouds → rain → back to rivers and sea.
**Groundwater** is stored deep underground; open land, soak pits and trees help recharge it.
Rivers flow **from higher to lower** ground; Luni ends in the Rann of Kutch.
Water plants and animals have **special features** – fins, floating leaves, waxy coating.

paper.what: Forms of water, fresh vs salt, name the animal
Why ocean water is not drunk; ways to get groundwater
Water cycle with a labelled drawing; how to recharge groundwater

sections.title: Draw it right
items: Water cycle: draw the sun, sea, clouds and rain with arrows going round.
Label each arrow: heating, vapour, clouds, rain.
Write one line under it: ‘The water cycle never stops.’

sections.title: Writing answers that score
items: Read the question twice and underline the key word (why, how, name, list).
Answer in full sentences using words from the book – e.g. ‘Microbes need moisture, air and the right temperature to grow.’
For ‘why’ questions, give the reason with ‘because’.
For 2–3 mark answers, write 2–3 separate points.
Add one example from the chapter (Godavari, Disha’s pickle, the green school) to show you understand.
Draw and label a simple diagram when it helps – the water cycle, types of teeth, the river’s journey.

sections.title: The day before the test
items: Read the key facts sheet aloud once.
Do the Play & learn activities again – if you get every card right first time, you are ready.
Take one Check knowledge quiz at Hard level.

checklist: I can explain why freshwater is precious.
I can name the three forms of water with examples.
I can draw and explain the water cycle.
I can say how groundwater is recharged.
I can name two water animals and two water plants with a feature.
exam.paperTitle: How this chapter is usually tested
exam.paperNote: Typical Class V school test pattern (1-mark MCQ, fill in the blanks, true/false and matching; 2–3 mark short answers; activity-based questions). Your school’s paper may differ slightly.

method: Built on how children learn best: start with a story or activity, sort and match ideas with your hands, say answers aloud before checking (active recall), and come back after 1, 3 and 7 days (spaced revision).
